text:
rita: heads-up — seeing a cluster of fncall validation REJECTs in eu-central. root request returns 200 OK but validation flags payload shape. console only shows 'validation failed' with no quick reason, which makes oncall triage slow.
paul: can you paste an example? is this the array-vs-object thing from last quarter?
rita: example (redacted): `{"tool":"user_lookup","result":{"users":[{"id":1}]}}` vs validator expecting `result` to be a single object `{...}` not an object-with-array. Some tool adapters sometimes wrap singletons in arrays.
noah: interesting — our streaming/coercion code has a path that turns a single item into an array for consistency, but we thought validator handled that via coercion rules. Looks like the validator rejects before coercion in some cases.
tess: console UX: we only show a link to the trace. Because rejects are sampled, traces often not accessible to SRE. We need a cheap reason string surfaced on the card (ops-visible) without leaking PII.
paul: telemetry issue: validation REJECT event sometimes lacks route_id/model_variant (older codepath). Without that, the rollout page can't correlate rejects to a variant -> teams think the model is fine.
rita: and billing: customers are being billed for the API call (success 200) but our internal tooling marks it rejected so rerankers/tooling don't run. Confusing for CS.
noah: proposal: add a minimal `validator_hint` enum to the validation event (values like array_wrapped, missing_key, type_mismatch) + an optional `sample_blob_id` for sampled sanitized payloads. Keep sample optional to avoid storage bloat.
tess: +1. For the console card show `validator_hint` and top-level failing path (e.g., `result.users`), and a "view sample (ops only)" link. Sample access flows through existing ACL.
paul: router change: we should support a per-route flag `allow_shape_coercion: on|off|canary(%)`. If on, we coerce arrays->objects for specific keys before validation. Canary mode flips coercion for X% traffic and emits `is_coerced` telemetry.
rita: BUT we must avoid masking regressions; coercion should set `coercion_applied=true` and increment a metric that triggers alert if >Y/minutes for canary. Also ensure canaryed coerced requests still show up in reject dashboards.
noah: implementation notes: 1) validator pipeline order: change to run a lightweight shape matcher that can emit `validator_hint` before hard reject 2) coercion should be a transform step that sets metadata, not silent patching 3) telemetry schema needs `validator_hint`, `coercion_applied` (bool), `route_id`, `model_variant`, `sample_blob_id` (optional).
tess: UX follow-ups: add filter in rollouts view for `validator_hint=array_wrapped` and show per-variant counts. Add quick action to toggle `allow_shape_coercion` for a route.
paul: billing: update runbook and billing docs to state that token billing follows the server response code; validators don't change billing. Also add a reconciler job to tag disputed events for CS.
rita: security note: sample_blob must be sanitized and TTL-limited. Use existing S3 bucket with lifecycle + ACL. No raw PII.
noah: CI: i'll add unit tests for validator hint emission and e2e test for coercion flag. We should run a canary with `allow_shape_coercion=canary(1%)` on canary-route-7.
ops-bot: Created task ENGPLAT-1302: add validator_hint enum & optional sample_blob_id to validation telemetry.
ci-bot: Canary scheduled: canary-route-7 @ 03:00 UTC with 1% traffic.
tess: action list: (1) noah PR for validator hint + transform ordering (2) paul PR to router for allow_shape_coercion flag + metrics (3) rita UI patch to surface hint + sample link (4) ops add billing note to runbook.
rita: thanks — sync tomorrow 10:00 CET to review canary telemetry.
